purpose: Census of load-bearing COUNT assertions in sections/*.tex not covered by check_prose_vs_evidence.py (MIN_DP=3, decimals only) or gate_count_claims.py (7 hand-registered CLAIMS).

audits.claim: Among 17 designated damaged cells in four model families ... the honest aggregate is 15/17 at or below the floor
audits.how_recomputed: dmg=[c for c in cells_mmlupro if not c['is_intact']]; len(dmg)==17; sum(1 for c in dmg if not c['above_floor'])==15
audits.load_bearing: THE headline claim. This number replaced the retracted 14/15 today; if wrong the paper's central aggregate is wrong.

audits.claim: 10/12 damaged non-OLMo cells read above chance; under naive 0.10, 12/12 do. Yet only 1/12 clears the best-constant floor
audits.how_recomputed: non=[c for c in cells_mmlupro if not c['is_intact'] and c['family']!='olmo2_7b']; len(non)==12; sum(above_chance_mean)==10; sum(above_chance_naive)==12; sum(above_floor)==1
audits.load_bearing: the wrong-null flip's point-estimate column; all three integers recompute exactly.

audits.claim: all 21 evaluated cells are powered at the scale of the reference effect
audits.how_recomputed: len(cells_mmlupro)==21 and sum(c['powered'] for c in cells_mmlupro)==21
audits.load_bearing: the power disclosure the paper says is mandatory; also the 21 = 17 damaged + 4 intact identity that exposed the retracted 15-denominator.

audits.claim: the designated set gives 9/85 cells above their floor against 45/85 above chance
audits.how_recomputed: len(cells_offmmlu)==85; sum(c['above_floor'])==9; sum(c['above_chance'])==45
audits.load_bearing: second headline flip; 85 = 17 arms x 5 benchmarks is the cardinality identity the denominator gate asserts.

audits.claim: all nine are healed arms retaining at least 14 of 32 layers
audits.how_recomputed: ab=[c for c in cells_offmmlu if c['above_floor']]; len(ab)==9; all(c['family']=='olmo2_7b' for c in ab)==True; all(c['retained_layers']>=14)==True
audits.load_bearing: this is what replaces multiplicity correction (concentration of exceptions). If any of the nine were a truncate-only arm the pattern claim dies.

audits.claim: 0/15 OLMo-2 cells at 12 layers or fewer and 0/60 truncate-only cells at any depth clear a floor; 25/60 read above chance; 7/60 significantly below; 52/60 underpowered
audits.how_recomputed: o12=[c for c in cells_offmmlu if c['family']=='olmo2_7b' and c['retained_layers']<=12]; len(o12)==15, sum(above_floor)==0. no=[c for c in cells_offmmlu if c['family']!='olmo2_7b']; len(no)==60, sum(above_floor)==0, sum(above_chance)==25
audits.load_bearing: the 0/15 and 0/60 are the contrast that makes the depth threshold non-trivial; 25/60 recomputes exactly (it is NOT 45-9).

audits.claim: the smallest above-floor margin among the nine is +6.47 points while the largest point estimate among the 76 at-or-below cells is +2.61
audits.how_recomputed: below=[c for c in cells_offmmlu if not c['above_floor']]; len(below)==76; max(floor_delta_pp)==2.6115; min over above-floor==6.4701
audits.load_bearing: the non-overlap claim; 85-9=76 and both extremes recompute.

audits.claim: five from shortgpt16 (+11.21 to +49.66, every cell at p=0.0001) and four from keep14 (+6.47 to +18.69, p<=0.0005; its fifth cell, PIQA at +2.61, is at the floor)
audits.how_recomputed: per-arm groupby on cells_offmmlu: shortgpt16 5/5 above, deltas [11.21,24.32,30.20,31.14,49.66] all p=0.0001; keep14 4/5 above, deltas [6.47,7.00,9.40,18.69] p in {0.0001,0.0005}
audits.load_bearing: the 5+4=9 decomposition; both ranges and both p-bounds are exact.

audits.claim: Fifteen of the 17 cells are at or below the floor / the two cells that clear the floor ... and the remaining 15 are at or below it (tab_mmlupro caption, 'over all 17 designated damaged cells')
audits.how_recomputed: tab_mmlupro prints 14 rows but the Llama-3 row collapses 'k14--k8' = 4 cells; per-family expansion gives OLMo-2 5 + Llama-2 4 + Llama-3 4 + Qwen3 4 = 17, non-OLMo = 12. A row count would say 14 and be wrong.

audits.claim: Four of the five designated damaged OLMo-2 cells are likewise above either chance line but not above the floor; the fifth, shortgpt16, is above both
audits.how_recomputed: olm=[c for c in cells_mmlupro if not c['is_intact'] and c['family']=='olmo2_7b']; len(olm)==5; sum(c['above_chance_mean'] and not c['above_floor'] for c in olm)==4 (keep14,keep12,keep10,keep8); shortgpt16 above_floor and above both chance lines

audits.claim: Seven of the ten cells that read 'above chance' were never above chance by any tested standard --- their intervals cover zero
audits.how_recomputed: counts_12_damaged_non_olmo: above_chance_point=10, above_chance_ci=3 -> 10-3=7
audits.load_bearing: this is the sentence that quantifies the paper's own self-correction of an inflated effect.

audits.claim: the flip is 3/12 above chance versus 1/12 above the floor
audits.how_recomputed: counts_12_damaged_non_olmo.above_chance_ci==3, .above_floor_ci==1, .n==12; harness self-validated by reproducing published v1 delta on 15/15 and published CI to <1e-14
audits.load_bearing: the symmetric-standard correction; the abstract calls it 'about a third of the size'. 3/10 -> the qualitative phrase also holds.

audits.claim: under Benjamini--Hochberg at q=0.05 --- or Bonferroni --- neither reference retains a single cell (0/12 both sides) ... observing 3 or more rejections out of 12 has binomial probability 0.0196
audits.how_recomputed: multiplicity_20260815.BH_q05_rejections and .bonferroni_rejections (read directly); binomial_P_X_ge_3 field
audits.load_bearing: if BH retained even one cell the 'undefined rather than 3/12 vs 1/12' framing would be wrong.

audits.claim: only two of the eight letter constructs (MMLU, BoolQ) have floors a balanced null could not produce; on the remaining six the floor lies inside the estimator's own sampling noise
audits.how_recomputed: parse tab_nulls data rows -> 9 rows, 8 distinct construct names (MMLU-Pro twice, one row per chance convention); rows with p<1e-5 = {MMLU,BoolQ} = 2 constructs; 8-2 = 6 remaining CONSTRUCTS (but 7 remaining ROWS)
audits.load_bearing: the abstract's census. NOTE the row/construct distinction is the trap: 9 rows / 7 non-significant rows vs 8 constructs / 6 non-significant constructs. Both prose sites correctly use the construct unit. This one IS covered by gate_count_claims.py (3 of its 7 entries).

audits.claim: The hazard covers five of the table's nine rows --- four distinct constructs, since MMLU-Pro contributes a row under each chance convention --- and not the two whose p moved ... The remaining rows are genuinely clean: OpenBookQA's floor is exact at 138/500, and ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge and CommonsenseQA round down
audits.evidence_file: sections/tab_nulls.tex + Fraction arithmetic on (stored 6dp floor, n)
audits.how_recomputed: for each row: cnt=round(floor*n); hazard iff stored_float > cnt/n. Hazard = {MMLU-Pro naive, MMLU-Pro item-avg, MMLU, PIQA, BoolQ} = 5 rows / 4 constructs. Clean = {OpenBookQA exact 138/500, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, CommonsenseQA round down} = 4 rows. 5+4=9. The two whose p moved (ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge) are indeed in the clean set.
audits.load_bearing: this paragraph is the paper's own disclosure of a downward-biasing convention; getting the row/construct split wrong would look like concealment. All four assertions in the sentence recompute.

audits.claim: all 27 pass the integrity gate; the permutation and bootstrap decisions disagree on 0/27 cells; six cells have q_BH<=0.05 and five clear Bonferroni at alpha/27=0.001852; 0/27 cells are significantly below the permutation null
audits.how_recomputed: 27 data rows parsed; sum(q<=0.05)==6; sum(p<=0.001852)==5 (all five are the p=0.0001 anchors); sum(delta<0 and p<0.05)==0 -> 0/27 below null; keep14 p=0.0172 sits at rank 7 and 7*0.05/27=0.0130 so q=0.0663 > 0.05 while qwen3/k14 q=0.0297 <= 0.05
audits.load_bearing: 0/27 is what dissolves H_family in 07_limitations; the 6-vs-5 split is what separates the surviving downgrade from the non-surviving upgrade in 5.3.

audits.claim: The 16 rows and their status are the retraction/narrowing ledger
audits.how_recomputed: count lines matching ^\s*\d+\s*& in tab_claims.tex == 16, and the last row number is 16 (no gaps)
audits.load_bearing: low-medium: a self-describing table count. Would be embarrassing but not conclusion-changing.

audits.claim: Table~\ref{tab:mmlupro} is the MMLU-Pro letter read-out for all 12 cross-family cells against the always-A floor
audits.how_recomputed: tab_mmlupro's own caption says 'over all 17 designated damaged cells'; expanding its rows (OLMo-2 5 rows + Llama-2 4 + Llama-3 'k14--k8' collapsed row = 4 + Qwen3 4) gives 17. 12 is the NON-OLMo subtotal only, i.e. it silently drops the five OLMo-2 rows that are physically printed in the very table it is describing (shortgpt16, keep14, keep12, keep10, keep8).
audits.load_bearing: SAME CLASS AS THE RETRACTED 14/15. This is the last surviving pre-remedy narrowed denominator: the R1-01 remedy was full inclusion of the five OLMo-2 arms, and 09a_relocated.tex:24 promises 'any damaged arm excluded from that denominator is named at the point of exclusion'. Here five arms are excluded and none is named. A reviewer who reads the appendix pointer then counts the table finds a 12-vs-17 contradiction inside the same appendix, and the paper's own integrity promise broken a second time.

audits.how_recomputed: f_const=1403/12032=0.11660572; slack=0.002992021 (=36/12032). sum(1 for r in tab_v2_full if acc_hat < f_const-slack)==13; 27-13==14; the 14 span {Llama-2,Llama-3,OLMo-2,Qwen3}=4 base models; of them 5 are 'heal@' cells with acc_hat spread 0.0341 pp
audits.load_bearing: this is the paper deflating its OWN 27/27 evidence claim; if 13 were wrong the self-deflation would be miscalibrated. All four integers (13, 14, 4, 5) recompute from the shipped table.

audits.claim: the per-stratum argmax is B, E, B, E for n_opt=5,6,7,8 (4 of 8 strata, 623 of 12032 items), giving 1439/12032 and a gap of exactly 36 items, or 0.299 pp ... 94.8% of its weight lies in A-argmax strata
audits.how_recomputed: per_stratum: 8 strata; those with argmax_L!='A' are n_opt in {5,6,7,8} with argmax B,E,B,E -> 4 of 8; sum(n_s) over them = 52+93+158+320 = 623; A-argmax weight = 11409/12032 = 94.82%; 1439-1403 = 36 items = 0.2992 pp

audits.claim: sixteen damaged cross-family cells have accuracy equal to the marginal of the emitted letter to machine precision (05_analysis) / Sixteen damaged cross-family cells ... (09a_relocated), both introduced as 'The most vivid SMALL-BENCHMARK cases'
audits.how_recomputed: universe = families[f].rungs[r!=base].tasks[t].interfaces.letter over the 5 evidence tasks; emit=argmax(pred_hist); marginal from task_letter_nulls[t].gold_letter_marginal/n; criterion of the source verdict (GATE2_CROSSFAMILY_VERDICT.md:5e) = modal_pred_share>=0.99 AND abs(acc-marginal)<1e-12. Over the 5 EVIDENCE tasks this yields 9. It yields 16 ONLY if Winogrande is added to the universe: modal>=0.99 goes 19->28 (matching the verdict's '28 damaged non-OLMo cells') and exact goes 9->16. Seven of the sixteen are Winogrande cells: llama2/k12, llama2/k14, llama3/k12, llama3/k14, llama3/k8, qwen3/k10, qwen3/k12.
audits.load_bearing: 09a_relocated.tex:24 states 'Winogrande is the sole negative control and ENTERS NO DENOMINATOR', and 04_experiments.tex:5 repeats it. This count silently puts 7 negative-control cells into a headline count, and both host sentences frame them as 'small-BENCHMARK' evidence for the paper's constant-emitter thesis. Excluding the control gives 9 (or 10 if MMLU is admitted, 12 without the modal>=0.99 filter). A reviewer who checks this finds the paper's own exclusion rule violated in the direction that makes its illustration look 78% more abundant. Note also that the source verdict's own printed table lists only 7 of the 16 rows, so the number was never auditable from the .md alone.
